headline: 'I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I'll have to. You will know soon enough.' + 'locked
dek: Asked about renewed US strikes on Iran, Trump said Iran 'can't do anything on its nuclear program without our approval', that the US must now decide whether to 'go further... and certify it...
sources: Donald Trump, remarks to reporters in the Oval Office, Thursday Nov 5; reported by Israel National News and Times of Israel liveblog
fault_line: Finish the job now while the US is 'locked and loaded' — or take the Qatar deal and certify no nuclear weapon? Commenters split on whether 'you'll know soon enough' is a real deadline or another tease.

sections.what_happened: Asked about renewed US strikes on Iran, Trump said Iran 'can't do anything on its nuclear program without our approval', that the US must now decide whether to 'go further... and certify it... so that it will never happen again', and: 'I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I'll have to. You will know soon enough.' He added: 'If we have to do the rest of the Iran thing, we're very much locked and loaded.'
sections.what_verified: Times of Israel liveblog (T3) quotes the remarks verbatim from the Oval Office session; Al Jazeera (T2) carried the quote as a headline/graphic ('Trump on Iran: You'll know soon enough') — AJ-branded graphic in the demand file and AJ 'Today's latest' headline listing; Israel National News reports the identical quotes (no declared tier in the registry — reported with attribution, NOT counted toward corroboration); Times Now liveblog relays the same quotes (no declared tier — not counted).
sections.what_disputed: Counterpoint: this is a decision tease, not an order — no strike order is confirmed. On Tuesday Nov 4 Trump told the FT he had 'no immediate plans' to strike; Wednesday he said he would do it all again. The diplomatic track runs in parallel: Iran's nuclear proposal via Qatar is under US review (0100-03) and Vance is pushing mediation; WSJ reported Trump privately sceptical Iran would meet his demands and expecting renewed bombing after the midterms. The quote's 'rest of the country' phrasing also echoes his Sept UNGA 'annihilate' threat — rhetoric, not a target list.
sections.why_matters: Trump, a day after losing Congress over the war, tells the Oval Office: 'maybe I'll have to destroy the rest of the country — you'll know soon enough.' Decision-tease frame; pair with the carrier gap (Roosevelt not before mid-Nov, 0300-02) as the clock.

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump, a day after losing Congress over the war, tells the Oval Office: 'maybe I'll have to destroy the rest of the country — you'll know soon enough.' Decision-tease frame; pair with the carrier gap (Roosevelt not before mid-Nov, 0300-02) as the clock. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Finish the job now while the US is 'locked and loaded' — or take the Qatar deal and certify no nuclear weapon? Commenters split on whether 'you'll know soon enough' is a real deadline or another tease.
